_comment: Shared by tools/room/build.py (where each CRT goes) and src/crts.ts (where the camera stops). crts is one entry per station, in tour order: Work is the CRT that used to be MediaSafe's, Projects is the bench TV, About me is the CRT that used to be Contact's (the code matches a TV's place in crts to its station). spares are the three other CRTs: lit glass with no station, no card and no click. bakeOrder is the ids of all six TVs in the order tools/room/build.py bakes them, which is the order of their random draws (a sticky note's colour, a keyboard's tilt): keep it, or a re-bake redraws them. Site axes in metres: x across, y up, +z toward the door. yaw is the way a CRT faces, in degrees: 0 faces +z, 90 faces +x. keyboard: false leaves out the keyboard where there is no surface in front of the CRT. panel (site only, no re-bake) pins the station text to that point instead of the CRT, to keep the subject in view. portrait (site only) is how much further back the camera stands on a portrait window. phone (site only) replaces that with its own portrait stop: camera, look and panel pin, to bring lit parts of the room into a phone's frame. A spare's camera and look are only for build.py's --preview renders. overview (site only, no re-bake) is the camera, look and vertical field of view (fov, degrees; the stations use CAMERA_FOV) of the opening view of the room, with an exit point the flights leave it through, chosen so every station's glass is in frame at 16:9 and 16:10 and in front of the camera; overviewPortrait is its pose for a portrait window, a shot of the lit parts of the room. props (read by tools/room/build.py too, which stands each new or moved prop where its entry puts the lit face, #380) is one entry for each prop the overview's framing rule names, the surfaces drawn on props at runtime and the click targets (the room has exactly two clicks, the rack and the desk phone): id, kind, centre (x, y, z in metres, the middle of the prop's lit face), yaw (degrees, as a CRT's: the way the face points, 0 toward +z, 90 toward +x), size (width, height in metres, along the face) and, if the face leans, tilt (degrees its normal is raised above level, default 0). kind is surface (a canvas plane drawn on the prop; the ids are #378's list: oscilloscope, rack-lights, iron-wisp, fan, radio, desk-phone, clock, laptop), board (the whiteboard, drawn on at runtime), target (a click target, the only two: rack and desk-phone-target, the whole desk phone, base and handset, a flat 0.20 x 0.285 m box over it, tilt 90, for #386 to place its 44 px target from; desk-phone above is only the display) or prop (framing only, no click: racket, ball-tube). Nothing but these entries places a plane or a target, and no later ticket edits them. oscilloscope, rack, rack-lights and iron-wisp equal where build.py puts those props (the scope screen 1.2 cm in front of its face and the rack lights 1.2 cm in front of the rack's front, at z -1.40, as the check probes put them; the wisp the probe's five points along x 1.44, z -0.8 and 0.06 m wide by choice). For the others build.py works its own sizes back from the entry: fan is the blades' axle (the blades' front is 0.03 m in front of it), radio the face of the radio on the middle shelf, desk-phone its display (on a keypad panel sloped 75 degrees; desk-phone-target the box over the whole phone: its base 0.20 x 0.22 m and the handset along its left side, which reaches 3 cm past the base at each end), clock the face (case and ticks baked, no hands: a surface draws them), laptop the opened screen (lid at 105 degrees), whiteboard 0.48 x 0.36 m on the back wall, racket the head and grip (leaning) and ball-tube the standing tube with the ball out of it, both only framed. src/visit/room-props.test.ts sweeps the overview's framing rule over them.
